principles.title: Understand the work before judging the solution
Make intended behavior and evidence inspectable
Keep people able to understand and recover

criteria.title: Bound the task
criteria.requirement: Name the workflow, one unit of work, start and end boundaries, context, AI role, exclusions and a current/manual/non-AI alternative.
criteria.check: Ask a second person to describe the review's boundaries, then compare their answer with the scope record.
criteria.pass_example: Review one intake request from receipt to advisor confirmation; exclude live sending.
criteria.failure_example: Make our business AI-ready without naming a task.
criteria.verification: Required fields plus accountable human scope review

criteria.title: Observe the current workflow
criteria.requirement: Retain an observed baseline and a connected current-state map with actors, normal work, exceptions, recovery, time, volume and an endpoint. Mark reported paths separately.
criteria.check: Follow a recent case through every step; reconcile elapsed time, labor and the sampling window. Inspect where work changes hands or returns for correction.
criteria.pass_example: A work log supports measured labor; a separate operator account describes an exception not observed in that sample.
criteria.failure_example: The owner guesses hours saved without knowing today's steps or work volume.
criteria.verification: Graph and numeric checks plus direct observation review

criteria.title: Connect requirements to an actual need
criteria.requirement: Connect each need to an owned, checkable requirement. Use distinct original work or end-user sources at the required risk depth.
criteria.check: Ask whose difficulty the requirement resolves, what would count as success, and whether two sources share the same origin.
criteria.pass_example: An operator discussion and a work record independently support preserving data after cancellation.
criteria.failure_example: Two summaries of one conversation are presented as two independent customers.
criteria.verification: Reference, origin and source-kind checks plus human relevance judgment

criteria.title: Include the people who bear the consequences
criteria.requirement: Name affected roles, including non-operators. Screen access/usability, privacy/security, unequal effects and human agency. Link applicable concerns to requirements and validation; justify inapplicable items with an owner and evidence. Human use/control cannot be excluded.
criteria.check: Ask who might be unable to use, correct, decline or challenge the workflow, and who could be affected without operating it. Inspect the linked success conditions and supporting evidence; a checked box alone is insufficient.
criteria.pass_example: A requester and an advisor can correct an intake; the requirement specifies retained data, readable error feedback and a human escalation path.
criteria.failure_example: The owner saves time, but a requester cannot correct a wrong generated record and nobody evaluated that effect.
criteria.verification: Deterministic coverage and applicability checks plus human/context-specific review; not an accessibility, fairness, privacy or security certification

criteria.title: Explain form, fit and function
criteria.requirement: Every requirement names what is represented, how it fits the surrounding workflow, what it must do and the reference material used to judge it.
criteria.check: Compare the artifact with its reference material to judge whether its role and behavior meet the requirement.
criteria.pass_example: A review form is linked to required intake fields, advisor responsibilities and cancellation rules.
criteria.failure_example: A finished-looking screen is accepted without knowing its purpose or reference requirements.

criteria.title: Trace the exact artifact to a check
criteria.requirement: Each important requirement/artifact pair has an executed check bound to both its exact artifact digest and its requirement/context fingerprint. A change to acceptance criteria, scope, linked states, references, dependencies or authority invalidates the affected check.
criteria.check: Compare both fingerprints with the record captured when the check ran. Repeat the affected check after a change; computing a new hash does not constitute retesting.
criteria.pass_example: A cancellation walkthrough records the exact screen revision and the field-preservation result.
criteria.failure_example: An agent edits error handling after tests ran, but the old test pass is reused.
criteria.verification: Deterministic chain and revision checks plus inspection of execution evidence

criteria.title: Distinguish simulated from implemented behavior
criteria.requirement: Label each requirement's behavior as specified only, simulated or implemented. Do not label a walkthrough of a simulation as an implementation test.
criteria.check: Identify the connected components and the mocks. Judge functionality from evidence of behavior, independently of visual polish.
criteria.pass_example: The export button is simulated; the review checks the intended recovery behavior and funds only implementation of that behavior.
criteria.failure_example: A mock success screen is presented as proof that a payment or export completed.
criteria.verification: Behavior-status and test-level consistency plus human inspection

criteria.title: Cover normal, edge and recovery states
criteria.requirement: Represent connected normal, edge and recovery paths with an entry, resolvable next-state IDs, reachable endpoints, data treatment, ownership and requirement links. Review transition conditions, dependency failures and bounded retry/exit behavior.
criteria.check: Try missing input, empty results, delay, unavailable dependency, cancellation and resumption where relevant. Document which cases apply.
criteria.pass_example: A failed save keeps entered data and explains how to retry or return to manual work.
criteria.failure_example: The happy path works but a failed save silently discards the user's input.
criteria.verification: State/reference checks plus context-specific human walkthrough

criteria.title: Make human and automated authority explicit
criteria.requirement: Record what people and automated components may access, change or send. Review approval, interruption, escalation and recovery boundaries. If AI only created the artifact, say so.
criteria.check: For an agent action, ask who authorizes it, how to stop it, what happens after partial completion and who resolves exceptions.
criteria.pass_example: A draft-only agent cannot send; an advisor approves changes and can return to a saved record.
criteria.failure_example: An agent may delete or message externally without a stated owner, approval boundary or recovery path.
criteria.verification: Required boundary review plus specialist verification when risk demands it

criteria.title: Count human oversight work
criteria.requirement: Estimate disjoint review, correction, escalation, rework and residual manual minutes with an owner and basis. Distinguish gross from net benefit.
criteria.check: Subtract every oversight component from gross labor savings. Keep waiting time and labor time separate. Leave missing baseline ROI indeterminate.
criteria.pass_example: Fifteen minutes of gross savings and fifteen minutes of oversight are reported as zero net time savings.
criteria.failure_example: Only generation speed is counted while a person must check and rewrite every output.
criteria.verification: Required fields and arithmetic plus human estimate review

criteria.title: Scale depth before starting
criteria.requirement: Classify six risk dimensions and four consequential-context flags. Use the highest dimension or context floor. Safety/rights impact or irreversible external action sets high; sensitive data or untrusted input to actions sets at least moderate. Any unknown prevents QUICK6.
criteria.check: Review consequence, reversibility, complexity, importance, impact and mission before choosing the path. Do not lower the classification to fit the meeting's length.
criteria.pass_example: A consequential allocation workflow goes to FULL even when its interface has only one screen.
criteria.failure_example: A simple-looking UI is treated as low risk despite an irreversible outcome.
criteria.verification: Deterministic routing plus competent human risk classification

criteria.title: Resolve findings at the required depth
criteria.requirement: Review reference defects, findings and unresolved risks. Unresolved critical findings cannot be waived. Add independent review and deeper plans when the risk tier requires them. A recorded human evidence-quality review must address relevance, completeness, authenticity and test adequacy; agent-only assertions cannot replace it.
criteria.check: Inspect each unresolved finding; passing other gates cannot offset it. Verify reviewer independence for moderate/high risk.
criteria.pass_example: A critical data-loss defect stays visible even when the baseline is also missing.
criteria.failure_example: A critical finding is marked accepted to obtain a favorable readiness result.
criteria.verification: Finding status and evidence checks plus reviewer judgment

criteria.title: Limit the engineering commitment
criteria.requirement: Record an owner, bounded engineering step, resource limit and next review trigger. Explain any investment despite a nonpositive net estimate; obtain separate owner authorization.
criteria.check: Ask what the team may build next and what it may not do yet. Retain a separate dated owner decision.
criteria.pass_example: One engineer-day for a disposable prototype, with no live sending and a review before further work.
criteria.failure_example: A gate pass is treated as permission for unrestricted building or deployment.
criteria.verification: Recorded bounds and rationale; authorization remains a separate human act

criteria.title: Separate effort from performance
criteria.requirement: Record preparation, timed-session and reporting burden. Keep protocol cost, projected operating oversight, reviewer judgments and actual system performance separate.
criteria.check: Check units and which activity each number measures. Do not infer operational accuracy, safety or readiness from document completeness.
criteria.pass_example: An expensive evaluation is reported separately from the workflow's projected operating cost.
criteria.failure_example: A high checklist score is reported as evidence that the implemented system works.
criteria.verification: Separate contract fields and arithmetic; no combined score

criteria.title: Preserve evidence and disclosure boundaries
criteria.requirement: Retain exact versions, source origins, digests and previous-run links. Preserve missing and stopped records. Keep private identities/comments out of public materials without permission.
criteria.check: Check whether another reviewer could reconstruct the run and whether each proposed disclosure is permitted. Retain the old record when creating a new run.
criteria.pass_example: A new FULL record links to the stopped QUICK6 record; private notes remain outside the public package.
criteria.failure_example: A synthetic example is relabeled as an actual pilot or private feedback is published as an endorsement.
criteria.verification: Structural provenance checks plus human permission review; hashes alone do not prove truth
